analysis.title: Woodward Inc. (WWD): F4Q26 earnings callback; Buy
key_insights: GS hosted a group investor meeting with Woodward's Director of Investor Relations on top-line growth drivers in aerospace and industrial, margin inputs, free cash flow and capital deployment. GS rates WWD Buy.
Woodward's initial 2027 Aerospace guide is 8-13% yoy revenue growth with an adjusted operating margin of 23.8-24.3%.
GS ranks the 2027 Aerospace growth drivers by magnitude: Aerospace OE, Aerospace aftermarket, Defense OE, Defense aftermarket.
In Aerospace OE, LEAP and GTF continue to ramp as narrowbody build rates rise at Boeing and Airbus. Woodward also has content gains outside narrowbody.

Aerospace aftermarket: spare LRU sales are expected at a level similar to 2026. Legacy engine services revenue is at a 'high plateau' and expected to stay there near term, though it has surprised to the upside in recent years. LEAP and GTF services revenue is growing faster than the industry average.
Excluding spare LRU sales, new-generation engine services revenue has nearly reached legacy, and the company expects it to cross over soon.
Defense has incremental OE drivers on various platforms. Defense aftermarket revenue stays lumpy quarter to quarter.
The long-term 30-35% incremental margin target for Aerospace remains in place. 2027 investments (new locations, work transfers) are meant to raise productivity later.
Beyond 2027, Woodward sees a $50mn (150 bps) margin benefit from recurring savings plus the reversal of this year's investment spending, with normal incrementals and productivity gains on top.
Woodward's initial 2027 Industrial guide is 1-5% yoy revenue growth with an adjusted operating margin of 18.2-18.7%.
The China On-Highway wind-down is a ~$110mn headwind to 2027 Industrial revenue. Excluding it, GS estimates the guide implies ~8-12% core Industrial growth.

Power Generation OE is the largest Industrial growth driver, supplying the data center buildout and electrification (could be high-teens % or better). Oil & Gas grew ~mid-teens % last year and is expected to grow about the same in 2027. Marine Transportation is expected up yoy but faces difficult comps, particularly in services.

The 2027 Industrial margin guide of 18.2-18.7% compares with a 2026 core Industrial margin of ~18.5%, not the reported 19.6%, because China OH was accretive to 2026 margin. Sales mix and growth investment hold core margin roughly flat.

Power Generation OE growth pressures near-term margin but builds an installed base for long-duration, high-margin services. Woodward is not forecasting Marine services to stay at recent elevated levels, particularly 2H26, which shifts mix toward OE.

Interest expense rises yoy from converting revolver balances to structured debt, higher overall debt and higher rates. 2027 CapEx of $290mn includes ~$70mn remaining for Spartanburg and is similar to 2026.
Proceeds from two divestitures (Pilot Controls and Santa Clarita product lines) are expected to be around $350mn and could fund additional share repurchase.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised its 12-month target to $487 from $478, based on 27.5X 2027E EV/EBITDA, implying 49.1% upside from $326.56. Growth drivers are Aerospace OE and aftermarket plus Power Generation OE for data centers.

earnings_insights: Woodward 2027 initial guidance (company, per IR meeting): Aerospace revenue +8-13% yoy with adjusted operating margin 23.8-24.3%. Industrial revenue +1-5% yoy with adjusted operating margin 18.2-18.7%.
GS estimates core Industrial growth of ~8-12% excluding the ~$110mn China On-Highway wind-down headwind.

GS estimates for fiscal years ending September (GS forecast, not reported): FY27E revenue $4,785.7mn, EBITDA $1,050.2mn, EPS $11.12. FY28E revenue $5,323.3mn, EPS $13.48. FY29E revenue $5,845.2mn, EPS $15.93.
FY26 (9/26) figures in the GS table: revenue $4,356.9mn, EBITDA $915.8mn, EPS $9.78.
GS quarterly EPS: 9/26 $2.83, then GS estimates of $2.37 for 12/26E, $2.60 for 3/27E and $2.83 for 6/27E.
risk_factors: Marine Transportation faces difficult comps, particularly in services, and Woodward is not forecasting recent elevated activity to continue.
Power Generation OE mix pressures near-term Industrial margins.
